Ugh. I went to a Chuck E. Cheese with my toddler for the first time since I was ten years old this year. I was so disappointed. It was nothing like I remember (from the 80's).

The theatre/animatronics part was gone and replaced by a wall of TV's. The games were just aweful content. There were actual Price is Right cosino games reconfigured for kids. The ball pit was gone, the rides are the same thing you find outside the grocery store...

The worse part was every ride or game is only one token. When I was a kid everything had a different value and you had to earn those tickets. I remember stressing the fuck out trying to do the math in my head at seven years old to figure out how to maximize what little tokens I had with the game that would give me the most tickets. I was learning economics without even realizing it. Now you hit a button with your one token and you get 30 tickets. There is nothing learned!

Also that dumbass rat comes out once an hour giving away free tokens and tickets. So just when you think you can leave, your kid gets sucked back in. It's terrible! It reminds me of Reno. We are not going to make it a regular treat for our kids. Thankfully in this day and age there are lots of other play options that cater to kids. ##### Please mark as "Creation"

The coming years would be cold ones. Thankfully, the microbes would see to it that the flora and fauna would change rapidly enough so that the inhabitants of Ebos would not starve, but Pomme wanted to remind the mortals, who would come out of this long winter stronger than ever, of the hope and life that Spring promised.

And so she created [Winter Berries](https://i.sli.mg/Cltd1p.jpg), which would come to be known by many names as time progressed and they took root in forests, grasslands, swamps and plains across Ebos. Beautiful [Golden Berries](https://i.sli.mg/kD4ewy.jpg) for the golden forest, pink [Mother Berries](https://i.sli.mg/oCv3NV.jpg) in the Rose Forest, and [red](https://i.sli.mg/Fpp10E.jpg) or [black](https://i.sli.mg/h98283.jpg) berries growing everywhere else. The flavors and characteristics may differ slightly, but they would be recognizable by all, especially the red, which would contrast most against the starkness of winter. Their vines would aggressively grow up any tree or shrub or grass, so that they would always be in a prime position to collect sunlight. Their roots will be invasive and they will grow not only in the wilds but also on walls within cities and other seemingly odd places. Outside of cities they would be abundant, growing in all biomes.

These berries will be immune to the frost and will thrive at temperatures lower than other plantlife on Ebos. When the winter is gone, the berries will either die or evolve because of the evolutionary microbes.

They are extremely sweet and dense with sugars, making them a high calorie snack for travelers, foragers, and excellent ingredients for fermented beverages, baked goods, and other preserves.

The Golden Berries and Mother Berries will take on the attributes of the Golden Forest and Rose Forest, respectively, meaning Golden Berries boost overall health and provide natural immunity to disease, while Mother Berries boost actual Savagery like the dew drops and Hummers of the Rose Forest, in addition to their normal nutritional value.

#####For those who don't know: currants are delicious in jams and jellies. My grandparents had beautiful old vines of both red and black currants on their homestead and Bertha's black currant jam was always one of my favorites. They both died last summer and and my parents had to sell the property, but damn if I'll never forget plum and currant jam in the Christmas packages, picking endless strawberries and raspberries, making poppy rolls (they grew the most lovely [peony poppies](https://i.sli.mg/fBaQN7.jpg)), and S'mores around the campfire <3
